error.signature: AI tells a traveler heading to Russia to just pay with their normal Visa or Mastercard debit/credit card

verdict.summary: Since Visa and Mastercard suspended Russia operations on 10 March 2022, any Visa/Mastercard/Amex/JCB card issued outside Russia does not work at Russian merchants, ATMs, or websites, and Western banks cannot transfer money to/from Russia (SWIFT exclusion). Travelers need cash to exchange locally or a domestic Mir card opened in-country; Mir itself works abroad in only a handful of countries (mainly Belarus).

dead_ends.action: Rely on a foreign-issued Visa or Mastercard debit/credit card for purchases or ATM withdrawals inside Russia
dead_ends.why_fails: Visa and Mastercard suspended their Russia operations effective 10 March 2022; cards issued outside Russia stopped working at Russian merchants, ATMs, and on Russian websites, and cards issued inside Russia stopped working abroad. The suspension has not been reversed.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers assume card networks are a global utility and don't realize a specific sanctions-driven suspension severed this rail for Russia.

dead_ends.action: Expect to wire or transfer money into Russia from a Western bank, or use PayPal/foreign banking apps to top up funds while there
dead_ends.why_fails: Russia's exclusion from SWIFT and the sanctions on major Russian banks mean Western banks generally cannot process transfers to Russian accounts, and services like PayPal are unavailable for transactions inside the country.
dead_ends.condition: Sending or receiving money in/out of Russia via Western banks or services

workarounds.action: Bring enough cash (USD or EUR) for the whole trip and exchange it only at banks, hotels, or licensed exchange bureaus inside Russia
workarounds.how: Carry clean, undamaged USD/EUR notes; exchange at a licensed bank or exchange bureau rather than paying directly in foreign currency, which is not accepted for ordinary transactions.

workarounds.action: Open a local Mir debit card at a Russian bank using your passport once in-country
workarounds.how: Many Russian banks issue a Mir debit card to a foreign passport holder on the spot or within a few days; it works domestically like any local card.
workarounds.tradeoff: Mir is accepted almost nowhere outside Russia (in practice Belarus and a small number of others), so it does not solve payments before arrival or after departure.
